- docs/plans/opencode-review-autofix-cutover-plan.md:lines 415-416 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The aggregate bullet claims "both 5/6 runs surfaced as the existing `non_retryable` class", but the diff's own table contradicts this. Run 4 (line 397, 33298934878) records "pass-2 dropped one slot without an alert; cause not in logs" — the cause is explicitly unknown, not the `non_retryable` class. Run 9 (line 402, 33328474242) records a context-window overflow on the mistral slot, which is a different failure signature from the deepseek `non_retryable` rows (lines 394, 401).
  WHY: This section is the audit-trail record of the "no new failure classes" gate leg. Mischaracterizing an unknown-cause reviewer miss and a context-window overflow as the known `non_retryable` class overstates what the run logs actually showed and undermines the forward audit trail this section now serves as.
- docs/plans/opencode-review-autofix-cutover-plan.md:lines 8-9, 57, 80, 458-459, 470-481 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new evidence section records that the `@stable` hold was lifted on 2026-08-30 before the Q3:A criterion was met, but every other statement of that gating rule in the same file is left unamended. Line 57 ("`@stable` ... tagged only after the parity criterion passes"), line 80 (same), line 458-459 ("gated by F2:A: `@stable` is tagged only after the production criterion passes"), and Rollout step 5 ("Hold `@stable`: do not run the mark-stable/release flow until the Q3:A criterion passes", lines 470-472) all still present the hold as the live, unconditional rule. Only the evidence section notes the deviation.
  WHY: A reader (or a future orchestrator/reviewer consuming this plan as a contract) reading the Decision table, Risks, or Rollout sections gets a rule the recorded audit trail directly contradicts, with no pointer to the deviation. The plan internally documents two mutually exclusive states of the same gate.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===
